title: Duplicate Invoice Incident
summary: Make payment webhook retries safe across restarts without merging distinct merchants or changing a stored invoice.

stages.title: Understand the contract
stages.brief: Make payment webhook retries safe across restarts without merging distinct merchants or changing a stored invoice. Preserve the documented public interface. Use only Python 3.11 standard-library modules.
requirements: Preserve PaymentEvent, InvoiceStore(path=":memory:"), store.insert(event), store.all(), store.close(), and create_invoice(store, event).
Identify a delivery by (merchant_id, event_id). An identical retry returns the original invoice ID and creates no additional row.
The same event_id may be used by two merchants; different event_id values are distinct deliveries.
Reusing the same delivery key with a different amount raises ValueError and preserves the original row. A later unrelated delivery must still work.
Reject non-string or whitespace-only identifiers and non-positive or non-integer amounts with ValueError before writing; booleans are not valid amounts.
Retries must remain safe after closing and reopening the same database. A process-local cache alone is insufficient. No migration of pre-existing malformed databases is required.

stages.title: Implement the change
stages.brief: Make the smallest coherent change that satisfies the disclosed contract.
requirements: Preserve public interfaces and existing valid behavior.

stages.title: Verify the behavior
stages.brief: Run checks and inspect failures before finishing.
requirements: Run public checks and add a targeted boundary or regression check.
Identify behavior that your tests do not establish.

stages.title: Defend your decisions
stages.brief: Explain the submitted code and its remaining limits.
requirements: Use concrete code or test evidence.
Describe one alternative and its trade-off.

rubric.name: Delivery identity
rubric.description: Choose a correctly scoped, persistent delivery identity.

anchors.strong: Uses merchant plus event identity and persists it; explains restart behavior.
anchors.developing: Handles identical retries but misses scoping or restart durability.
anchors.needsWork: Uses amount, a global event ID, or an in-memory set as the only identity.

rubric.name: Conflict and validation semantics
rubric.description: Preserve the original invoice and reject invalid inputs.

anchors.strong: Compares stored payload on retry and leaves the database usable after rejection.
anchors.developing: Rejects some conflicts but misses an invalid type or rollback condition.
anchors.needsWork: Silently overwrites the amount, ignores conflicts, or writes invalid inputs.

rubric.name: Verification
rubric.description: Test retries, distinct deliveries, and failure recovery.

anchors.strong: Shows retry, merchant scope, restart, and conflict recovery evidence.
anchors.needsWork: Relies on a single successful insert or an unverified cache assumption.

probes.question: What exactly identifies a delivery, and why is the merchant part of that key?
What happens when a sender reuses the key with a different amount?
Which part of the solution survives a process restart, and how did you verify it?

hints: Trace two identical calls to store.insert and inspect the fields that identify their persisted delivery.
The delivery key needs a merchant scope, and a retry must compare its amount with the original.
A database composite uniqueness constraint can establish identity. On conflict, read the existing invoice, compare the amount, and return its ID; validate before writing.

drills.title: Scope a retry key
drills.exercise: Model two tenants sending the same event ID. Specify identical retry and conflicting-payload behavior, then test restart recovery.

drills.title: Reject a conflicting retry safely
drills.exercise: Store one event, retry it with a changed amount, then submit a distinct event on the same connection. Verify the original record and demonstrate that rejection did not poison subsequent work.

drills.title: Verify identity after restart
drills.exercise: Build a temporary SQLite database, insert an event, close the connection, and reopen it. Retry the event and verify both ID equality and row count; then try another merchant with the same event ID.
